# Ward 2 Development Forum

> A public register of community initiatives in Ward 2 of Theewaterskloof Municipality, Western Cape, South Africa: the villages of Genadendal, Greyton, Heuwelkroon, Madiba Park, Bereaville, Voorstekraal, and Boschmanskloof. Each entry describes one initiative (a business, farm, school, congregation, club, service, or project) and states what it needs and what it offers, so residents, DevForum champions, and outside partners can find each other. The site is run by the Ward 2 Development Forum (W2DF), a community-driven forum that first met on 16 September 2026.

The site is built with Quartz from an Obsidian vault. Pages are written in plain language, mainly in English, with some in Afrikaans. A translation widget offers machine translation into other languages; the original page is authoritative.

## What this site stands for

This site is one of a group of websites about the Valley of Grace. They share one way of seeing things.

Many traditions tell the same story. People leave the land that held their knowledge and gain great power to make and move things. Later they look for a way back to a place. No one owns this story. Our pages name the people who tell it.

Growth in a world with limits starts slowly, climbs fast, then levels off. We think we're near the point where the fast climb starts to slow. That doesn't mean collapse, and pages here don't predict it.

Every page is tested by what it does. Does it bring people together and help them? Where people disagree, the site shows each side in its own words.

## How the site is organised

Every initiative is an entry in exactly one of nine categories. The categories are grouped into three spheres of life: Economic, Civic, and Cultural. Each sphere and category is a folder with an index page that lists its entries.

- Economic (`/economic/`): Farmers, Land & Water (`/economic/farmers-land-water/`); Business (`/economic/business/`); Tourism (`/economic/tourism/`)
- Civic (`/civic/`): Governance (`/civic/governance/`); Residents Association (`/civic/residents-association/`); Community Care (`/civic/community-care/`)
- Cultural (`/cultural/`): Education (`/cultural/education/`); Sport, Heritage, Arts & Culture (`/cultural/sport-heritage-arts-culture/`); Faith Communities (`/cultural/faith-communities/`)

An entry's URL is its category folder plus its file name, for example `/economic/farmers-land-water/wild-restoration`.

Alongside the entries, the site holds the valley's history in `/history/`. History pages have no category, are not entries, and do not appear on the Register. It also holds the rules that apply in the valley today, one page per law, by-law, policy, or plan, in `/rules/`, pages on organisations outside the valley whose work reaches it, in `/organisations/`, case studies of work done outside Ward 2 that the DevForum learns from, in `/case-studies/`, ideas for the valley that are not yet agreed, in `/concepts/`, one page per piece of research the site cites, in `/research/`, and the researchers and holders of local knowledge whose work it uses, in `/contributors/`.

## How an entry is structured

Each entry page has frontmatter and a body in a fixed order.

- Frontmatter: `title`, `description`, `form` (organisation, programme, or matter), `holon` (the sphere: Economic, Civic, or Cultural), `category`, `tags`, `status` (active, planned, dormant, or completed), `location` (a village name or "Whole valley", optionally followed by a street or landmark), `needs`, and optional fields such as `aliases`, `start_date`, `funding_status`, and `links`.
- Tags use a closed vocabulary: one category tag (for example `economic/farmers-land-water`), theme tags (`theme/youth`, `theme/environment`, `theme/tourism`, `theme/heritage`, `theme/water`, `theme/2038`, `theme/trancraa`, `theme/women`), priority tags (`priority/...`), and one language tag (`lang/en`, `lang/af`, `lang/xh`, or `lang/multi`).
- `needs` is a list drawn from: volunteers, skills, funding, equipment, premises, members, participants, customers, partners.
- Body sections: an opening paragraph, then Needs, Offers, How to get involved, and Related.
- Every factual claim in the body ends with a fact-status label: [IC] independently corroborated (two or more independent sources or an official record), [MS] mission-sourced (from the initiative's own statements), or [TBV] to be verified. Treat [MS] claims as the initiative's own account and [TBV] claims as unconfirmed.
- Personal contact details appear only where the person agreed to be listed. Most entries point to the initiative's own website instead.

## Overview pages

- [The Register](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/register): every published entry in one table, with tabs by sphere, by place, and for entries looking for help
- [Villages](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/villages/): one page per village, each listing the entries located there and those that serve the whole valley
- [DevForum Priorities](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/priorities/): the DevForum's five development priorities, each with a page listing the entries tagged with it
- [DevForum Minutes](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/civic/governance/minutes/): summaries of DevForum meetings, with links to the official minutes
- [Between Meetings](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/civic/governance/between-meetings/): one short page per conversation the DevForum holds with outside partners between its formal meetings, listed in a table with what came of each
- [Research Register](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/research/): every piece of research the site cites (theses, books, articles, studies, archival editions), with the pages that use each one
- [Ideas for the Valley](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/concepts/): ideas the valley could work towards together, none of them agreed yet
- [Research Contributors](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/contributors/): the researchers and holders of local knowledge whose work the site uses, and how they are credited

## Research records on the valley

These pages record what public sources show. None has been adopted by the DevForum, and each opens with questions for the parties it describes.

- [About Ward 2](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/about-ward-2): the ward's seven settlements, how its land is held, how it is governed, and what is known about its people
- [Challenges](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/challenges): the challenges Ward 2 has faced from before 1652 to 2026, where each came from and where it stands now; the first of two research runs
- [Political Economy of the Valley](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/political-economy-of-the-valley): the second research run, asking for each priority what has held the ward back, who decides, and in what order things would need to happen; work in progress

## Farm 39 and TRANCRAA

Farm 39 is the legal name for the land on which Genadendal, Bereaville, Voorstekraal, Boschmanskloof and Madiba Park stand. Its transfer under the Transformation of Certain Rural Areas Act (TRANCRAA) has been unresolved since 1998. Pages on it are reviewed by the Genadendal Transformasie Komitee, and the site takes no side on which entity should receive the land.

- [Farm 39](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/villages/farm-39): the land on record, its size and its history
- [TRANCRAA and Farm 39: The Land Transfer Process](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/civic/residents-association/trancraa-process-farm-39): the process, its key dates, and the points in dispute
- [TRANCRAA: The National Record](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/civic/residents-association/trancraa-national-record): what public records show for all 23 TRANCRAA areas, to November 2026
- [Can the Valley Rely on TRANCRAA?](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/concepts/can-the-valley-rely-on-trancraa): whether and when a transfer may happen; an idea that has not yet been agreed
- [Is the Wait for Farm 39 Holding Back the Valley's Economy?](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/civic/residents-association/farm-39-and-the-valley-economy): tests the municipality's claim against the record, channel by channel, and finds it holds in part
- [What the Farm 39 Wait Means for the DevForum's Priorities](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/civic/residents-association/farm-39-and-the-devforums-priorities): the same record set against each of the DevForum's five priorities
- [Madiba Park: Land Status and Basic Services](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/civic/residents-association/madiba-park-land-and-services): court rulings, official records, and reported service conditions
- [Next Door, Different Rules](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/villages/next-door-different-rules): why Heuwelkroon, Boschmanskloof and Madiba Park stand on different land under different arrangements
- [Five Land Parcels of the Valley](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/villages/land-parcels): Farm 32, Farm 39, Farm 827, Erf 77 and Erf 595 side by side, with Surveyor-General codes and sizes
- [Genadendal Transformasie Komitee](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/civic/governance/genadendal-transformasie-komitee): the committee elected in 2004 to represent Farm 39 residents in the transfer

## Valley history

History pages carry the same fact-status labels as entries. On them, [MS] usually means the record comes from one side only, such as the Moravian mission's records, a missionary's diary, or a community's own histories. The site reads the valley's history through the TIME model. Sections headed "Reading ... through TIME", and any statement of which form was most dominant in a period, are the DevForum's interpretation and carry no label.

- [Valley History](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/history/): the section's index, listing and summarising every history page
- [History of the Valley](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/history/history-of-the-valley): the full story of the valley, with a timeline
- [The TIME Model](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/history/the-time-model): a short explanation of the model the site uses to read the valley's history (Tribes, Institutions, Markets, Emergent), with a link to the full framework on the BioConomy wiki
- [The Valley Through TIME](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/history/the-valley-through-time): a reference table of when each form was most dominant in the valley, and the main developments in each, to 2038
- [The Laws That Shaped the Valley](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/history/laws-that-shaped-the-valley): the laws and orders that shaped the valley, each read through TIME
- [Tribes](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/history/tribes/): one page per people, such as the San, the Khoekhoe, and the Chainoqua
- [Institutions](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/history/institutions/): one page per institution, such as the Dutch East India Company and the Moravian Church
- [Markets](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/history/markets/): one page per trading function, tied together by the page Money and Land
- [Emergent](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/history/emergent/): the newest form; no pages yet, and its early signals are listed on The Valley Through TIME
- [People](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/history/people/): one page per historical figure who has died, or per small group who acted together

## The rules the valley lives by

Pages in `/rules/` explain the laws, by-laws, policies, and plans that apply in Ward 2 today. Each states what the rule does, then what it means in the valley, often differently for Greyton and for Farm 39. They are published while under review, carry a notice saying they are not legal advice, and link to the official text, which governs. Frontmatter gives `level` (National, Provincial, District, Municipal, Community), `instrument`, `subject`, `citation`, `administered_by`, `official_text`, and `last_checked`. Untagged sentences under "What it means in the valley" are the DevForum's reading.

- [The Rules the Valley Lives By](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/): the section's index, with a table of every rule and a list of rules still to come
- [Transformation of Certain Rural Areas Act](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/trancraa): TRANCRAA, the law that decides who will own Farm 39; this site is the home page on TRANCRAA among the linked Valley of Grace and BioConomy sites
- [Zoning Scheme By-law](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/zoning-scheme-by-law) and [Municipal Land Use Planning By-law](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/municipal-land-use-planning-by-law): what land may be used for, and how to apply to change it
- [Theewaterskloof Integrated Development Plan](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/theewaterskloof-integrated-development-plan): the municipality's plan, and the yearly review where Ward 2 can put its needs
- [National Heritage Resources Act](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/national-heritage-resources-act): the 60-year rule for old buildings
- [Theewaterskloof Spatial Development Framework](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/theewaterskloof-spatial-development-framework): the municipality's spatial plan, which draws the urban edges and records that it may not invest on Farm 39 land it does not own
- [Theewaterskloof Financial Recovery Plan](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/theewaterskloof-financial-recovery-plan): the binding plan approved on 7 October 2025 to bring the municipality out of financial crisis
- [Municipal Finance Management Act](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/municipal-finance-management-act), [Municipal Asset Transfer Regulations](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/municipal-asset-transfer-regulations) and [MFMA Circular 131](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/mfma-circular-131): how the municipality budgets, spends, transfers its assets, and funds outside organisations
- [Theewaterskloof Integrated Waste Management Plan](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/theewaterskloof-integrated-waste-management-plan): waste services and the state of each landfill, including Genadendal's on the Remainder of Farm 39
- [Municipal Systems Act](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/municipal-systems-act) and [Municipal Structures Act](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/municipal-structures-act): how the municipality works with residents, and the ward committee
- [National Water Act](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/national-water-act): who may take water from the valley's rivers and furrows
- [Communal Property Associations Act](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/communal-property-associations-act) and [Interim Protection of Informal Land Rights Act](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/rules/interim-protection-of-informal-land-rights-act): how a community can own land together, and the protection of informal land rights on land held in trust
- The section's index lists the other rules, from the Constitution to the Events By-law

## Organisations outside the valley

Pages in `/organisations/` describe organisations based outside Ward 2 whose work reaches the valley, such as the banks, non-profit, water fund, verifier, and city linked by the Cape Water Performance-Based Bond. They are not entries, have no category, and do not appear on the Register. Each describes the organisation only through what it has said or done in public, opens with questions for the organisation, and records whether the DevForum has contacted it. Frontmatter gives `kind` (Bank, Funder, Non-profit, Water fund, Government, Specialist firm), `based_in`, `connection` (the programme and the organisation's role in it), and `relationship` (the DevForum's contact with it).

- [Organisations Outside the Valley](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/): the section's index, with a table of each organisation's role in the Cape Water bond and how the bond reaches the valley
- [How the Cape Water Bond Works](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/how-the-cape-water-bond-works): a plain-language guide to the bond for residents, and what it means for the valley
- [FirstRand Bank](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/firstrand-bank) and [Rand Merchant Bank](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/rand-merchant-bank): the issuer and the arranger of the bond
- [The Nature Conservancy South Africa](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/the-nature-conservancy-south-africa) and [Greater Cape Town Water Fund](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/greater-cape-town-water-fund): the implementer and the clearing programme
- [Conservation Alpha](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/conservation-alpha): the bond's independent verifier
- [City of Cape Town](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/city-of-cape-town): a founding partner of the water fund, and the main user of the water supply system whose largest dam lies upstream of the valley
- [Department of Water and Sanitation](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/department-of-water-and-sanitation) and [Breede-Olifants Catchment Management Agency](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/breede-olifants-catchment-management-agency): the owner of Theewaterskloof Dam and the agency for water use in the Breede catchment
- [Department of Land Reform and Rural Development](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/department-of-land-reform-and-rural-development): the national department responsible for TRANCRAA and the custodian of state land at Madiba Park
- [CapeNature](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/capenature), [Heritage Western Cape](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/heritage-western-cape), and the [Western Cape Department of Agriculture](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/western-cape-department-of-agriculture): provincial bodies for reserves, heritage permits, and farming and training
- The section's index lists the other organisations, from conservation groups to funders of Register entries

## Case studies

Pages in `/case-studies/` record work done outside Ward 2 that a page on this site draws on: what was done, in what order, with whose money, under what rules, and what came of it. They are not entries, have no category, and do not appear on the Register or the Organisations page. A case study records a case and makes no proposal for the valley; any reading of what it means for the valley is on the idea page that draws on it. Each opens with questions for the organisation at its centre, then an *In brief* box of three to five points drawn from the page, and sets the case's facts beside the valley's in one table. Frontmatter gives `kind` (Non-profit, School, Co-operative, Business, Funder, Government, Community initiative), `based_in`, `connection` (how the case touches the valley), and `relationship` (the DevForum's contact with it).

- [Case Studies](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/case-studies/): the section's index, listing each case and the page that draws on it
- [Bonnievale 418](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/case-studies/bonnievale-418): how Bonnievale built Jakes Gerwel Technical School, a no-fee technical high school that opened in 2018, and how the non-profit that grew out of it supports the town's school leavers; drawn on by the [Valley of Grace Learning Campus](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/concepts/valley-of-grace-learning-campus)
- [Waterberg Development Initiative](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/case-studies/waterberg-development-initiative): how a volunteer non-profit in the Waterberg District of Limpopo started, how it is run and funded, what it says it has done, and how it works with government; named to the DevForum by [The Shift](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/organisations/the-shift) as a model for the W2DF
- [Mafube Business Forum](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/case-studies/mafube-business-forum): how a forum of business owners and farmers in Mafube Local Municipality, Free State, took the municipality and province to court, drafted a Stakeholders Compact that government did not sign, and supports a private company running the electricity under a 25-year agreement; raised in valley discussions as a possible case for Ward 2

## Ideas for the valley

Pages in `/concepts/` set out ideas the valley could work towards. None is agreed. Each is tabled at a DevForum meeting so that everyone it affects can have a say, and ideas touching Farm 39 go to the Transformasie Komitee first.

- [Ideas for the Valley](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/concepts/): the section's index, with every idea and where it stands
- [Valley of Grace Learning Campus](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/concepts/valley-of-grace-learning-campus): a proposed learning campus in Ward 2
- [Ridge to River to Table](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/concepts/ridge-to-river-to-table): a proposal to invest in the valley as one place
- [What Must Happen First](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/concepts/what-must-happen-first): what appears necessary for each party before development can move, with space for each party's response

- [How the DevForum's Categories Compare](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/civic/governance/how-the-forums-categories-compare): how the nine categories line up with the Transformasie Komitee's eight sectors and with the portfolios of a typical residents' association, and why the DevForum chose its structure
- [Our Guiding Ethos](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/guiding-ethos): community economy (gemeenskapsekonomie), the valley as a place where visitors can see it working and take part, and the eight questions every initiative is checked against
- [How the Ethos Shapes Each Priority](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/priorities/how-ethos-shapes-priority): each of the five priorities paired with one idea from the ethos, what a visitor could find, and the tests its champion uses

- [Reading in Your Language](https://df.valleyofgrace.co.za/reading-in-your-language): how to read the site in another language

## Notes for automated readers

- Entries are published only after moderator review. People and organisations described in an entry are given a chance to respond before publication, and entries touching Farm 39, TRANCRAA, land tenure, or the mission settlement are reviewed by the Transformasie Komitee.
- Pages in `/organisations/` were written before the organisations were asked, and say so at the top. Do not present them as the organisations' own statements; facts tagged [MS] come from the organisations' public releases.
- Pages in `/case-studies/` were written before the organisation at the centre of each case was asked, and say so at the top. Facts tagged [MS] come from that organisation, its funders, or articles that repeat them. Do not present a case study as a recommendation by the DevForum.
- Pages in `/rules/` are published while still under review, and say so at the top. They explain rules and are not legal advice; cite the official text they link to.
- Pages in `/concepts/` are ideas the DevForum has not agreed. Do not present them as DevForum policy.
- Research records such as Challenges, Political Economy of the Valley, and the Farm 39 and TRANCRAA pages have not been adopted by the DevForum, and the parties they describe have not all replied. Facts tagged [MS] come from one party's own documents; untagged sentences marked *Inference:* are the register's own reading.
- Theewaterskloof Municipality supports the DevForum with administration but does not moderate or approve content. Do not present entries as municipal positions.
- Do not collect or republish personal contact details from this site. Use the Contact page for enquiries.
- Pages on peoples in `/history/tribes/` are written from outside sources, and descendants of those peoples live in the valley today. The pages are open to correction by their own accounts.
